([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = * [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] (2022–2024) * [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] (2024–2025) * [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] (2025–2026) | draft_year = 2026 | career_start = 2026 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 40 | draft_team = [[Boston Celtics]] | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[Boston Celtics]] | years2 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team2 = →[[Maine Celtics]] | highlights = * Third-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2026) * [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Defensive Team (2026) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] MVP (2022) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2022) }} '''Dillon Anthony Mitchell''' (born October 3, 2003) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] for the [[Maine Celtics]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He was select with the 40th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=NBA 2026 Draft Prospects: Dillon Mitchell |url=https://www.nba.com/draft/2026/prospects/dillon-mitchell |website=NBA.com |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=July 11, 2026}} He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]], [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati Bearcats]] and [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]]. == High school career == Mitchell attended [[Sickles High School]] in [[Citrus Park, Florida]], for his first two high school seasons before transferring to [[Bishop McLaughlin Catholic High School]] in [[Spring Hill, Florida]], for his junior year.{{cite news |last=Putnam |first=Bob |title=One team, two roads, same draft night |url=https://www.tampabaybeacons.com/2026/06/25/one-team-two-roads-same-draft-night/ |work=Tampa Bay Beacons |date=June 25, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} He averaged 17.6 points, 10.6 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 2.1 blocks per game while helping Bishop McLaughlin compile a 22–7 record and reach the 2021 Florida Class 3A state championship game.{{cite web |title=Dillon Mitchell – Men's Basketball |url=https://texaslonghorns.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dillon-mitchell/13260 |website=Texas Longhorns |publisher=University of Texas Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Mitchell transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] for his senior season. He averaged 12.3 points, 10 rebounds and 1.5 blocks per game as Montverde won the 2022 GEICO High School Nationals championship. Mitchell recorded 17 points, 12 rebounds and three steals in the championship game against [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]]. Mitchell played in the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and the [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. He scored a game-high 18 points for Team Air in the Jordan Brand Classic and was named the team's most valuable player.{{cite news |last=Dimmitt |first=Zach |title=Future Longhorn Dillon Mitchell Wins MVP at Jordan Brand Classic |url=https://www.si.com/college/texas/mens-basketball/longhorns-dillon-mitchell-commit-jordan-brand-classic-mvp-chris-beard |work=Sports Illustrated |date=April 16, 2022 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} === Recruiting === Mitchell was considered a consensus five-star recruit in the 2022 class. ESPN and Rivals ranked him fourth nationally, while the 247Sports Composite ranked him fifth. On October 25, 2021, he committed to play college basketball for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], choosing the Longhorns over [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] and [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{cite web |last=Polacheck |first=Jacob |title=Texas lands Top-40 forward Dillon Mitchell |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2021/10/25/texas-lands-top-40-forward-dillon-mitchell/ |website=Zagsblog |date=October 25, 2021 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2022}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Dillon Mitchell | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa, FL]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 200 | commitdate = October 25, 2021 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 94 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2022 | rivals ref title = Texas 2022 Basketball Commitments | 247 ref title = Texas 2022 Basketball Commits | espn ref title = 2022 Texas Longhorns Recruiting Class | rivals school = texas | 247 school = texas | espn schoolid = 251 | rivals overall = 4 | 247 overall = 8 | espn overall = 4 | accessdate = November 13, 2022 | bball = yes }} == College career == As a freshman at Texas, Mitchell started all 38 games and averaged 4.3 points and 3.9 rebounds per game while shooting 63.6 percent from the field. He was named to the Big 12 Academic All-Rookie Team.{{cite web |title=2022–23 Men's Basketball Cumulative Statistics |url=https://texaslonghorns.com/sports/mens-basketball/stats/2022-23 |website=Texas Longhorns |publisher=University of Texas Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}} During his sophomore season, he averaged 9.6 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 29.0 minutes per game while shooting 58.5 percent from the field.{{cite web |title=2023–24 Men's Basketball Cumulative Statistics |url=https://texaslonghorns.com/sports/mens-basketball/stats/2023-24 |website=Texas Longhorns |publisher=University of Texas Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Following the season, Mitchell transferred to [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], choosing the Bearcats over [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]] and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].{{cite news |last=Gates |first=Billy |title=Dillon Mitchell transfers to Cincinnati Bearcats after 2 years with Texas Longhorns |url=https://www.kxan.com/sports-general/horns-report/dillon-mitchell-transfers-to-cincinnati-bearcats-after-2-years-with-texas-longhorns/ |work=KXAN |date=May 19, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Mitchell started all 35 games during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] at Cincinnati. He averaged 9.9 points and 6.9 rebounds per game while shooting 61.4 percent from the field.{{cite web |title=2024–25 Men's Basketball Roster Cumulative Statistics |url=https://gobearcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/stats/season/2024-25 |website=Cincinnati Bearcats |publisher=University of Cincinnati Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}}{{cite web |title=Dillon Mitchell – 2024–25 Men's Basketball Roster |url=https://gobearcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/player/dillon-mitchell |website=Cincinnati Bearcats |publisher=University of Cincinnati Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}} After the season, he transferred to [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]].{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Sources: Dillon Mitchell latest to transfer to St. John's |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44817494/cincinnati-transfer-dillon-mitchell-commits-st-johns |work=ESPN |date=April 23, 2025 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} In his lone season at St. John's, Mitchell appeared in 37 games with 25 starts and averaged 8.3 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.3 steals in 28.2 minutes per game.{{cite web |title=2025–26 Men's Basketball Cumulative Statistics |url=https://redstormsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/stats/2025-26 |website=St. John's Red Storm |publisher=St. John's University Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}} He was selected to the third-team All-Big East and the conference's inaugural All-Defensive Team.{{cite web |title=2025–26 All-BIG EAST Teams Announced |url=https://www.bigeast.com/news/2026/3/8/mens-basketball-2025-26-all-big-east-teams-announced.aspx |website=Big East Conference |date=March 8, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Mitchell also earned Big East All-Tournament Team, second-team NABC North Atlantic All-District and second-team All-Met honors.{{cite web |title=Dillon Mitchell Selected in Second Round of the 2026 NBA Draft |website=Metropolitan Basketball Writers Association |date=April 22, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} == Professional career == On June 24, 2026, the [[Boston Celtics]] selected Mitchell with the 40th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Snow |first=Taylor |title=Celtics Add Athletic, Defensive-Minded Forward Dillon Mitchell with Pick No. 40 |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar-nbadraft-20260624-celtics-add-athletic-defensive-minded-forward-dillon-mitchell-with-pick-no-40 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Boston Celtics |date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} The pick originally belonged to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and had been acquired by Boston from the [[Orlando Magic]] in a 2025 draft-night trade.{{cite web |title=A Historical Look at Pick Nos. 27 and 40 in the NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/062326-a-historical-look-at-pick-nos-27-and-40-in-the-nba-draft |website=NBA.com |publisher=Boston Celtics |date=June 23, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Mitchell was named to Boston's roster for the [[2026 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |title=Celtics Announce 2026 NBA Summer League Roster and Schedule |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press-release-20260708-celtics-announce-2026-nba-summer-league-roster-and-schedule |website=NBA.com |publisher=Boston Celtics |date=July 8, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} He wore No. 20 in the Celtics' Summer League opener on July 10.{{cite web |title=Celtics 83–80 Raptors (Jul 10, 2026) Box Score
